- When sentiment is positive (≥0.25) in recent history, model tends to under-forecast upward momentum; adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior 30d mean.
- Model consistently over-forecasts early in the 30d horizon (especially days 1–5) after recent price spikes; reduce first 3–5 forecast points by 1–2%.
- After a sharp price spike (≥2% from prior 5-day high), model often overshoots in next 3–5 days; apply a 1–3% downward correction to forecast peak.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: if 30d forecast is below 65.00 and sentiment is neutral, increase forecast by 0.5–1.0% to avoid underestimating rebound.
- If sentiment history is flat (all 0.00), model tends to over-predict downward trend; apply a 0.5–1.5% upward bias to avoid false bearish signals.
- Forecast horizon 30d is prone to lagging by 1–3 days; if true outcome shows strong upward momentum on day 1–3, adjust forecast to reflect 1–2 day lead.
